componentAcceptance: A real independent Agent commits the file and succeeded operation before being SIGKILLed. The Host loses the reply and enters needs-reconciliation with outcome unknown. A normal Agent restart on the same dataDir preserves machineId and listens on a new loopback port. After endpoint re-pair and a read-only binding, the Host reconciles the original operation to succeeded with exactly one fs_write call, one operation row and unchanged file bytes. The focused test passes three consecutive runs and the related remote-write combination is 15/15.
productAcceptance: T14 passes at integration level: the network break after action start produces unknown and reconnect observes rather than re-executes the original operation. This is not a public-network production deployment or every-command acceptance. Formal scores are 0/20 work packages, 7/63 scenarios and M0 11/12.
testRuns: Focused real network reconnect test: three consecutive runs, each 1 test / 1 pass / 0 fail.
Network reconnect + remote-write suite: 15 tests / 15 pass / 0 fail.
Final npm test: phase one 1590/1586/0/4 and phase two 370/287/0/83; total 1959 tests, 1874 pass, 0 fail, 87 skipped.
preservedFailures: The first fixture treated a plain-text abort marker as JSON and never released the reply; this was corrected to a file-existence check.

The first re-pair used binding expectedRevision 1 even though re-pair had incremented it to 2, causing MACHINE_CONFIG_CONFLICT. The fixture now uses the actual revision; no product assertion was weakened.
limitations: The real network break is a loopback Agent process kill and restart, not a public WAN outage or protected production tunnel test.
This closes T14 remote write reconnect behavior, not every command/browser/desktop facade or mixed command-tree cancellation.
No real model inference, production process, push or release was used.
